issues.claim: ONE FIX with VAL-R5-03 (V07). Two binding texts written this round give two outcomes for a crossing station that a carried-down raised way holds on the town enceinte that becomes the village palisade. §2.7's support step (3) (l. 2560-2564), from R5-02's held-stretch clause, reads: '`wallToWay`, `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) and the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade (V07 §3.5a (4)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road'. V07 §3.12 (l. 2610-2615) says 'the standing fabric survives unchanged' and makes the palisade 'the innermost standing enceinte'. V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1611-1614), from VAL-R4-03's amended text, keeps the station in the palisade's line, 'its support the band's stretch under the deck … with its raised gate whose tower carries the deck … — the one gate at a support the palisade carries'. T-V7-48 counts that raised gate among the palisade's gates at supports. Under the base, the tower stands outside the gate law. Under V07, it is a gate of the palisade. The palisade's gate set feeds VS3 step 7's split, F-V-GATE ('a trace with no gate after VS4'), the siege's engines facing 'then the gates', `gatesAndKeep`'s 'the palisade's gates' and the crisis look's gate-passage keep-out (§10.2 (d); T-V7-69 (b)). So two builders build two outcomes. §2.7 (3)'s list is right for `wallToWay` and `absorbWall`, where the wall line goes; at the hand-off down the line stays.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3): replace 'and `wallToWay`, `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) and the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade (V07 §3.5a (4)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road, the enceinte's record kept while it stands' with 'and `wallToWay` and `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road, the enceinte's record kept while it stands; the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade keeps it in the palisade's line as the standing fabric it is (V07 §3.12) — a raised gate the one gate at a support the palisade carries, an aqueduct's arch no gate (V07 §3.5a (4))'. In the same step's parenthesis, replace 'a stretch laid after it — a village palisade's among them — takes no station' with 'a stretch laid after it — a village palisade VS3 lays after it among them — takes no station'. V07's side is VAL-R5-03.

issues.claim: MATRIX-GAP (the arch vault's door under a later wall), verdict undefined. repair-r5-V04's HAND-OFFS (l. 103-111) put this question to the adjudicator, and no unit closed it. §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2606-2608) has a wall stretch laid after a raised way end 'at a `vault` span … at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole'. V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1607) and T-V7-48 say the same of the palisade. 'A walled-up arch' is V04's own term for an arch vault with no door (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1): 'no door is made and `W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR` is reported (a walled-up arch)'). Yet V04 keeps the vault's one `door` at the midpoint of an open face. Its two open faces are the grade faces that take a seated building's entrance and windows (§3.5.4 (f); V03 §3.12 (9)). No reconcile runs for a later wall, since a later trace changes no `feet`, `supports` or `spans` (R5-02), and T-V4-63 now bars 'no arch vault changed by either'. The trace crosses both mouths, so wherever it crosses near mid-span the run's end meets the face over the door. This is common at CITY, where a later stage's ring meets an S4 viaduct whose spans inside the town are `land` vaults. Nothing states whether the door stays, moves or is walled up, or what it opens onto. One builder walls up both mouths, leaving the vault and any building seated in it unreachable; another keeps a door that opens into the wall's masonry. Principle (11) grades an undefined edge on a normal path as major.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d): replace 'at a `vault` span ending at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole' with 'at a `vault` span ending against its arch vault's two open faces (V04 §3.5.4 (f)), the chamber kept whole with its door — where the run's end would meet the door's face over the door, the door moves along that face to the nearest point clear of the run's band, in the commit that lays the stretch (a fate in a hand edit's dry run), and keeps opening onto the ground beyond it; the far face is closed by the run's other end —'. V04's END: (1) §3.5.4 (d) (1)'s door rule adds 'a door that a wall stretch laid after the raised way would cover moves along its face to the nearest point clear of the run's band (§2.7's support step (6) (d)), the chamber, its key and footprint unchanged; with no clear point on either face, no door, `W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR`'. (2) `ArchVaults.reconcile`'s trigger lists (§1b l. 328, §2.6's arch-vault row l. 867, §4.3's row l. 2577) add 'a wall stretch laid across a `vault` span's strip (its door only)'. (3) T-V4-63's 'no arch vault changed by either' becomes 'no arch vault's key, footprint or closure changed by either, its door moved clear of the run where the run met it', and its fixture's circuit crosses the `vault` span at its door. V07's END: §3.5a (4)'s 'at an arch vault ending at its two walled-up arch mouths' becomes 'at an arch vault ending against its two open faces, its door kept clear (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. If the adjudicator rules instead that the mouths are walled up and the door removed, V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) and (f) and T-V4-63 must say so in the same words.

issues.claim: ONE FIX with VAL-R5-01 (model). V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1604-1615) reads every palisade as 'a wall laid after the raised way (§2.7's support step (6) (d))' and keeps a crossing station only for a raised way carried down from a CITY. The base gives a crossing station to every raised way created across a standing wall, a hand aqueduct included: §7.1 (l. 10441-10443) reads 'a course meeting an enceinte's trace comes down to a ground vertex before it …, while an aqueduct crosses a wall by an arch in the curtain, never a gate'; §4.8 *Gates* (l. 7668-7673) has 'by hand an aqueduct, §7.1' take the crossing as a wall opening; and §2.7's support step (3) holds that station. The palisade is an `Enceinte` (V07 §3.4 step 7), and V07 (1) admits a hand aqueduct at every rung. So on a palisaded village, a hand aqueduct drawn across the standing palisade gets a station by the base. Its stretch is held while the deck stands, so V07 §3.4 (8)'s decay passes over it, and it is taken back into the line as its support whenever VS3 re-lays the trace (§2.7 (6)). V07 instead treats the station as 'a support whose `state` is absent', abuts it and calls it 'never a gate', with no station kept. A station no stretch lies under becomes a pier with its own ring and `state`, so the two builds differ in the `supports` record, in the decay and in V04's reconcile. V07 also calls the carried-down station's 'raised gate … or the aqueduct's arch' 'the one gate at a support the palisade carries', but the base says an aqueduct's arch is 'not a gate (no portal, no gate law)' (§4.8; V06 §3.7.6 (5)), and T-V7-48 counts only the raised gate. 'A raised way crossing the circuit makes no gate (its deck passes over)' holds only for a raised way the palisade is laid after, because a hand raised road comes down before the trace (§7.1). Separately, and minor: 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch' leaves out (6) (d)'s soffit cap.
issues.required_change: V07 §3.5a (4): (a) Replace 'The palisade is a wall laid after the raised way (§2.7's support step (6) (d)):' with 'A palisade laid after a raised way — VS3's trace at generation and at every derivation that re-lays it, or a palisade T3 `wall` draws — runs on beneath its deck (§2.7's support step (6) (d)):'. (b) Replace 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch' with 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch, its top no higher than the span's soffit (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. (c) Replace 'A raised way carried down (V07 §3.12) whose crossing station stands on the enceinte that becomes the palisade keeps that station as standing fabric — its support the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands, with its raised gate whose tower carries the deck or the aqueduct's arch (§2.7's support step (3)) — the one gate at a support the palisade carries.' with 'A raised way created across the standing palisade keeps its crossing station (§2.7's support step (3)). This covers a hand aqueduct, which crosses by an arch in the curtain (§7.1; a hand raised road comes down before the trace instead). It also covers a raised way carried down (V07 §3.12) whose station stands on the enceinte that becomes the palisade. The station's support is the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands and taken back into the line as its support at every derivation that re-lays the trace (§2.7's support step (6)). A carried-down raised gate, whose tower carries the deck, is the one gate at a support the palisade carries. An aqueduct's arch is no gate: no portal, no gate law (§4.8 *Gates*).' §3.17's row 'a raised way over the palisade' adds '; a hand aqueduct across the standing palisade crossing it at one station by its arch (V07 §3.5a (4))'. T-V7-48 adds 'a hand aqueduct drawn across the VILLAGE fixture's standing palisade — one crossing station on the trace, its stretch the station's support and held (no `breached` or `dismantled` there while the deck stands) through a village epoch whose decay breaches the palisade, no gate counted for its arch, and the station taken back into the line after Regenerate (keep)'. The model's side is VAL-R5-01.

issues.claim: R5-04 made one comparison for plan damage, stated at §6.3 (l. 10006-10008) and cited everywhere: the element is 'compared only from its entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b); for an element a restoring event's re-cut mints, the week that restoration ends …)'. R5-04's sweep said V04 needs nothing, but V04 §5.6's lead (l. 2888-2890) restates the comparison without the entry week: 'each plan element shown damaged while the decay level is above 0 and at least the element's keyed threshold (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s comparison; …)'. Likewise UE33's E1, 'a building never decayed (level 0) … draw byte-identically', lacks §8.6's new 'and under no disaster look' (l. 14157). V03 draws the plan and its damage, and UE33's E7 carries the look, so nothing built or tested changes.
issues.required_change: V04 §5.6's lead: replace 'while the decay level is above 0 and at least the element's keyed threshold (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s comparison;' with 'while the decay level is above 0 and at least the element's keyed threshold, compared from the element's entry week into the plan (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison; V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b);'. UE33's E1: replace 'a building never decayed (level 0)' with 'a building never decayed (level 0) and under no disaster look (§8.6)'.
